name: snarl-sopi-backend
description: Snarl and Sopi operator backend v6.32.1: find sales a machine made while its clock was wrong. 8626020716 came back from a reboot with the clock unset, stayed offline, and kept selling - so those sessions are stamped with a time that never happened, and searching the window they really occurred in finds nothing. Only receivedAt, stamped by this backend when the machine finally posted, means anything. v6.32 computed the closed-to-received gap with Math.max(0, ...), which clamped away exactly this case: a clock set into the future makes closedAt LATER than receivedAt, a negative gap that would have shown as 0s. It is now skewSeconds, signed, and a new clockSuspect marks a sale whose closedAt cannot be true - closed more than a minute after we received it, dated before 2020, or unparseable. Ordinary queueing is a large positive skew and is deliberately NOT flagged: the clock was right, the link was down. The panel strikes through a claimed time it does not believe, tints the row, counts the affected sales above the table, and offers a filter for them alone; the CSV carries skewSeconds and clockSuspect so the set can be matched to the card processor on amount and receipt time rather than on a timestamp that is fiction. Cumulative over v6.32.
